# web-core steps

Use web apps in real browsers, the way the people who use them do: open pages, fill in forms, click buttons and links, answer dialogs, download files, and check what the page shows.

Each web app is registered with its address:

```gherkin
Given the parcels web app with the following properties:
  | url | http://localhost:8400 |
```

The browsers run on the machine that runs axx. The pack drives Playwright 1.62.1, and downloads its browsers the first time a scenario uses each one. The web app can use another `engine` (`firefox`, `webkit`, or the Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge installed on the machine), and present the browser as a `device` (like `iPhone 15`), with a `viewport`, a `locale` and a `timezone`.

- **Pages.** `the {string} page is opened` opens a page of the app; the other steps act on it. A link that opens a new browser tab makes it the current tab, until it is closed.
- **Finding things.** Fields are found by their label (or, without one, their placeholder), buttons, links, tabs and menu items by their name, and text anywhere on the page, in every frame: the names people see. Names must match exactly. Where a name is not enough, a step takes a selector in its place: `css=…`, `xpath=…` or `testid=…`.
- **Waiting.** Every step waits for what it needs: an action for its element to be ready, a check for the page to show what it expects, 10 seconds unless `within {duration}` says otherwise. There is no step to sleep.
- **Dialogs.** A dialog the page opens (an alert, a confirmation, a question) waits for `the dialog is accepted`, dismissed or answered; other steps fail while it is open.
- **Isolation.** Each scenario has its own browser context: its own cookies and storage, so scenarios run in parallel.
- **Failures.** A failed step attaches a screenshot of the page. A failed scenario keeps a Playwright trace in `.axx/web/traces`, step by step, with the feature file: open it with `npx playwright show-trace` or at trace.playwright.dev.
- **Watching.** With `packs.web-core.watch: true` in axx.yaml, the browsers open in windows on your screen: watch the scenarios, and open DevTools. `slowdown` slows them down.
- **Pausing.** `axx run --pause-at <file>:<line>` pauses before a step, and `packs.web-core.pauseOnFailure: true` where a scenario fails, in Playwright's Inspector: resume, step through the browser's actions, pick an element, which the Inspector names as steps do (`the "Register" button`), or record what you do on the page as steps.
- **Sessions.** A web app can start signed in: `cookie.<name>`, `header.<name>`, `local storage.<key>`, `session storage.<key>`, and `username` and `password` for HTTP authentication, for the app's address only.
- **Secrets.** Take passwords and tokens from the environment, as `${env:…}`: whatever a step takes from the environment is shown as `********` in failures and traces.

Values in the steps and the table expand `${env:..}` and `${sys:..}`.

## `web-core.app`

```gherkin
Given the {word} web app with the following properties:
  | property | value |
```

Register a web app, and how the browser presents itself to it. The first web app registered is the default.

| Parameter | Takes | For example |
|---|---|---|
| `{word}` | one word, with no spaces | `parcels`, `PX-4101` |

| Property | Takes | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | where the browser finds the app; page paths are below it |  | _required_ |
| `engine` | the browser; `chrome` and `msedge` are those installed on the machine | `chromium`, `firefox`, `webkit`, `chrome`, `msedge` | `chromium` |
| `device` | a device Playwright knows, like `iPhone 15` or `Pixel 7`: its screen, user agent and touch |  | |
| `viewport` | the size of the page, like `1280x720` |  | `1280x720` |
| `locale` | the browser's language, like `de-DE` |  | `en-US` |
| `timezone` | the browser's time zone, like `Europe/Berlin` |  | `UTC` |
| `color scheme` | what `prefers-color-scheme` says | `light`, `dark`, `no-preference` | |
| `reduced motion` | what `prefers-reduced-motion` says | `reduce`, `no-preference` | |
| `media` | the media the page's styles are for | `screen`, `print` | `screen` |
| `user agent` | the user agent the browser sends |  | |
| `location` | where the browser says it is: a latitude and a longitude, like `52.5200, 13.4050` |  | |
| `permissions` | the permissions the app has, like `notifications, clipboard-read` |  | |
| `tls.verify` | `false` accepts the app's certificate, whatever it is |  | `true` |
| `username` | the username for the app's HTTP authentication, with `password` |  | |
| `password` | the password for the app's HTTP authentication, with `username` |  | |
| `cookie.<name>` | a cookie the browser starts with, for the app's address |  | |
| `header.<name>` | a header the browser sends the app |  | |
| `local storage.<key>` | an item of the app's local storage, from the start |  | |
| `session storage.<key>` | an item of the app's session storage, from the start |  | |

**Example:**

```gherkin
Given the parcels web app with the following properties:
  | url    | http://localhost:8400/portal |
  | engine | webkit                       |
```

_Since 0.1.1._

## `web-core.open`

```gherkin
When the {string} page[[ of the {word} web app]] is opened
```

Open a page of the web app: a path below its `url`, or a whole URL. The steps that follow act on this page. A page that answers with an error status (404, 500...) fails the step.

| Parameter | Takes | For example |
|---|---|---|
| `{string}` | text in double or single quotes, which the step leaves out | `"Get a quote"`, `'Express'` |
| `{word}` | one word, with no spaces | `parcels`, `PX-4101` |

**Variants**, the parts in `[[...]]` said or left out:

- `the {string} page is opened`
- `the {string} page of the {word} web app is opened`

**Example:**

```gherkin
When the "/quotes" page is opened
When the "/parcels/PX-4101" page of the portal web app is opened
```

_Since 0.1.1._

## `web-core.fill`

```gherkin
When the {string} field is filled with {string}
```

Type a value into the field with that label (or, without a label, that placeholder), replacing what it holds.

- Date fields take dates as `2026-10-01`.
- A value from `${env:…}`, such as a password, is a secret: failures and traces show it as `********`.

| Parameter | Takes | For example |
|---|---|---|
| `{string}` | text in double or single quotes, which the step leaves out | `"Get a quote"`, `'Express'` |

**Example:**

```gherkin
When the "Weight (grams)" field is filled with "1200"
When the "Password" field is filled with "${env:SHOP_PASSWORD}"
```

_Since 0.1.1._

## `web-core.key`

```gherkin
When the {word} key is pressed[[ in the {string} field]]
```

## `web-core.accept`

```gherkin
When the dialog is accepted
```

Accept the dialog the page shows (its OK): a message, a confirmation or a question. The page waits for an answer, so every other step fails while a dialog is open. The step waits for the dialog: 10 seconds.

**Example:**

```gherkin
When the dialog is accepted
```

_Since 0.1.1._

## `web-core.dismiss`

```gherkin
When the dialog is dismissed
```

Dismiss the dialog the page shows (its Cancel). The step waits for the dialog: 10 seconds.

**Example:**

```gherkin
When the dialog is dismissed
```

_Since 0.1.1._

## `web-core.answer`

```gherkin

```

Type an answer to the question the dialog asks, and accept it. The step waits for the dialog: 10 seconds.

## `web-core.dialog`

```gherkin
Then [[within {duration} ]]the dialog shows {string}
```

Check that the page shows a dialog with the text, as part of its message (case matters). The check waits for a dialog: 10 seconds, or `within {duration}`.

| Parameter | Takes | For example |
|---|---|---|
| `{duration}` | a duration in seconds (`s`) or minutes (`m`) | `5s`, `2m` |
| `{string}` | text in double or single quotes, which the step leaves out | `"Get a quote"`, `'Express'` |

**Variants**, the parts in `[[...]]` said or left out:

- `the dialog shows {string}`
- `within {duration} the dialog shows {string}`

**Example:**

```gherkin
Then the dialog shows "Cancel parcel PX-4101?"
```

_Since 0.1.1._

## `web-core.shows`

```gherkin
Then [[within {duration} ]]the page shows {string}
```

## `web-core.download.contains`

```gherkin
Then the downloaded {string} file contains {string}
```

Check that a file the browser downloaded holds the text.

- Case matters; runs of spaces and line breaks count as one space.
- The text is read by the file's type: the text of a PDF's pages, the paragraphs and tables of a Word document (.docx), the cells of an Excel workbook (.xlsx), or the text itself.

| Parameter | Takes | For example |
|---|---|---|
| `{string}` | text in double or single quotes, which the step leaves out | `"Get a quote"`, `'Express'` |

**Example:**

```gherkin
Then the downloaded "parcels.csv" file contains "PX-4101,Anna Weber,IN_TRANSIT"
```

_Since 0.1.1._

## `web-core.download.row`

```gherkin
Then the downloaded {string} file has a row where:
  | column | value |
```

Check that the table of a file the browser downloaded has a row with those values in those columns: a CSV or TSV file, or an Excel workbook (.xlsx, its first sheet), whose first row names the columns.

| Parameter | Takes | For example |
|---|---|---|
| `{string}` | text in double or single quotes, which the step leaves out | `"Get a quote"`, `'Express'` |

Each row names a column, as the file's first row names it, and the value the file's row has in it.

**Example:**

```gherkin
Then the downloaded "parcels-birch-and-bloom.csv" file has a row where:
  | Parcel | PX-WEB-5401 |
  | Status | REGISTERED  |
```

_Since 0.1.1._

## `web-core.element.shown`

```gherkin
Then [[within {duration} ]]the {string} {element} is shown
```

Check that the page shows the element: by the name people see, or by a selector (`css=…`, `xpath=…` or `testid=…`). The check waits for it: 10 seconds, or `within {duration}`.

| Parameter | Takes | Values | For example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{duration}` | a duration in seconds (`s`) or minutes (`m`) |  | `5s`, `2m` |
| `{string}` | text in double or single quotes, which the step leaves out |  | `"Get a quote"`, `'Express'` |
| `{element}` | a kind of element on the page, plural after a number (`buttons`): a `field` by its label or placeholder, an `option` is a radio button, an `element` is anything, by its text, label, alternative text or title | `button`, `field`, `checkbox`, `option`, `link`, `tab`, `menu item`, `element` | `button`, `field` |

**Variants**, the parts in `[[...]]` said or left out:

- `the {string} {element} is shown`
- `within {duration} the {string} {element} is shown`

**Example:**

```gherkin
Then the "Cancel the parcel" button is shown
Then within 5s the "css=.parcel-card" element is shown
```

_Since 0.1.1._

## `web-core.element.hidden`

```gherkin
Then [[within {duration} ]]the {string} {element} is not shown
```

Check that the page does not show the element, by its name or a selector. The check waits for it to go: 10 seconds, or `within {duration}`.

| Parameter | Takes | Values | For example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{duration}` | a duration in seconds (`s`) or minutes (`m`) |  | `5s`, `2m` |

- `within {duration} the {string} {element} shows {string}`

| `{string}` | text in double or single quotes, which the step leaves out | `"Get a quote"`, `'Express'` |

- `the browser sent a {word} request to {string}`
- `within {duration} the browser sent a {word} request to {string}`


## `web-core.clock.set`

```gherkin
Given the browser's clock is set to {string}
```

Set the time the web apps' pages see, from then on.

- The time is like `2026-09-25T14:00:00+02:00`, or `2026-09-25 14:00` in UTC.
- Time goes on from there, so the pages' timers still run.
- Set it before opening the pages whose timers a step moves forward.

| Parameter | Takes | For example |
|---|---|---|
| `{string}` | text in double or single quotes, which the step leaves out | `"Get a quote"`, `'Express'` |

**Example:**

```gherkin
Given the browser's clock is set to "2026-09-25T14:00:00+02:00"
```

_Since 0.1.1._

## `web-core.clock.forward`

```gherkin
When the browser's clock is moved forward by {duration}
```

Move the time the web apps' pages see forward, as if the computer slept that long.

- The timers due in between fire once, and what expires, such as a session, expires.
- The pages' timers are the browser's own from when its clock is set: set it before opening them.

| Parameter | Takes | For example |
|---|---|---|
| `{duration}` | a duration in seconds (`s`) or minutes (`m`) | `5s`, `2m` |

**Example:**

```gherkin
When the browser's clock is moved forward by 31m
```

_Since 0.1.1._
